description_text:
Description
Southall is a premier destination bringing nature, produce and people together in a powerful and unique way.

The Corporate Controller is responsible for directing all aspects of accounting, finance, and asset management for Southall. This role serves as the owner's financial representative who bridges Mishkin Family ownership goals with operational performance to maximize property value and return on investment. The position leads the planning, management, and achievement of financial objectives while providing strategic oversight on revenue strategies, operational efficiency, and capital projects. Areas of oversight include Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, Purchasing, Receiving, Audit, and Capital Planning. This position ensures Southall's mission, long-term profitability, asset appreciation, and sustainability by partnering closely with Southall CEO, General Manager, and Departments 

Responsibilities
The Corporate Controller will lead and develop the following positions:

• Director of Finance — Provides senior financial leadership and management oversight across all finance and accounting functions; works with department managers in achieving their respective budgets; serves as the primary deputy to the Corporate Controller
• Accounting Manager / Assistant Controller — Oversees day-to-day accounting operations, month-end close, and financial reporting support
• Accounts Payable & Payroll Supervisor — Manages vendor payments, expense processing, and payroll accuracy and compliance
• Accounts Receivable & Credit Manager — Oversees billing, collections, credit approvals, and guest/group account management
• Construction & Fixed Asset Accountant — Manages capitalization policy, fixed asset ledger, depreciation schedules, and accounting for ongoing construction projects and capital improvements
• Purchasing Manager — Leads procurement strategy, vendor relationships, inventory control, and receiving operations
• IT Manager — Supports information systems, property management system integration, and technology infrastructure
• Night Audit Supervisor — Manages overnight reconciliation, daily revenue reporting, and front office accounting interface
• Strategically lead Finance and Accounting operations to advance Southall's mission while safeguarding all company assets
• Develop, manage, and refine annual budgets and rolling forecasts to support sustainable growth
• Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting packages to drive profitability and inform strategic decision-making
• Own the full accounting cycle, including balance sheet management, income statements, accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll, and account reconciliations
• Lead audit preparation and coordinate with external auditors to ensure clean, efficient reporting
• Maintain and enforce the monthly controller's checklist and close calendar
• Establish and oversee inventory control systems and internal controls
• Develop and manage purchasing procedures, including turn ratios, days-on-hand benchmarks, and vendor performance across major asset categories
• Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local tax requirements, including sales, liquor, labor, and hotel taxes
• Review and manage leases, contracts, agreements, covenants, and restrictions to protect company interests
• Oversee accounting software integration with the Property Management System
• Maintain financial databases and management reporting tools
• Evaluate departmental productivity and drive continuous process improvement
• Partner with the Director of Finance to ensure seamless execution of day-to-day financial operations and team development across all accounting functions
• Lead performance management for all direct reports and their respective teams
• Act as the owner's representative, aligning operational decision-making with ownership objectives and long-term asset appreciation goals
• Monitor and analyze operational accounting, Net Operating Income (NOI), identifying opportunities to improve revenue, control costs, and enhance overall property performance
• Provide strategic oversight of capital expenditure planning, prioritization, and execution, ensuring projects are delivered on time, on budget, and consistent with asset value objectives
• Evaluate and benchmark operational and financial performance against competitive set and industry standards, recommending corrective actions where needed
• Partner with property leadership on revenue management strategies, including pricing, channel mix, and demand forecasting, to optimize RevPAR and total revenue
• Conduct regular property performance reviews, preparing ownership-level reporting packages that translate operational results into investment-level insights
• Assess and manage risk across the asset, including insurance, deferred maintenance, and capital reserves
• Support ownership in evaluating strategic decisions such as renovations, repositioning, or financing.
• Oversee the Construction & Fixed Asset Accountant in maintaining the fixed asset ledger, depreciation schedules, and capitalization records
• Establish and enforce capitalization policy in accordance with GAAP, ensuring proper distinction between capital expenditures and operating expenses
• Oversee accounting for all construction-in-progress (CIP) activity, ensuring timely and accurate project cost tracking and transfer to fixed assets upon completion
• Partner with project managers and ownership on construction budgets, draw schedules, and variance reporting
• Coordinate fixed asset physical inventories and reconciliations on a scheduled basis
• Ensure proper accounting treatment for disposals, impairments, and write-offs
• Support audit and tax preparation with fixed asset schedules, depreciation reports, and CIP documentation
Requirements

• 15+ years of progressive accounting, finance, and/or asset management experience, preferably in hospitality, real estate, or single-asset ownership environments
• Prior experience in a CFO, Controller, or Asset Manager role strongly preferred
• Demonstrated ability to lead and develop senior finance staff, including Director-level talent
• Strong technical accounting knowledge (GAAP) with demonstrated ability to manage complex financial operations, including fixed assets and construction accounting
• Working knowledge of hotel performance metrics, including NOI, RevPAR, ADR, and GOP
• Excellent leadership, communication, and organizational skills with the ability to present effectively to ownership
• Ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines in a dynamic environment
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; experience with ERP or property management systems a plus
• Master's degree in Accounting, Finance, or Real Estate preferred
• CPA and continuing education in accounting strongly preferred

Our Benefits
Competitive compensation package
Medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, company-provided life insurance
Generous paid time off accruals
9 paid holidays annually
Weekly pay
401k and company match
Education reimbursement
Best-in-class Employee Assistance Program
Free weekly outdoor activities and wellness classes
30% internal discounts
Fresh and free daily meal
Bountiful internal growth opportunities

Our Team

Assembled intentionally with dynamic expertise, the Southall team is offered the unique opportunity to learn humbly with, and from, each other. We invest in a growth mindset and take it upon ourselves to strengthen our knowledge and grit daily. We honor the cycles of nature, get our hands dirty and taste the earth’s bounty in an effort to connect with the land.

We plan with purpose, seeing past the present day and seeking to consider the planet with each step. We embrace a blend of ancient techniques and modern technologies in our practice of sustainability. We celebrate ingenuity and resourcefulness and approach our roles through the eyes of an entrepreneur, looking beyond our respective corners to the big picture.

Acting with intention, we approach each day with gratitude for the opportunity to serve our guests and each other. A humble holder of our Michelin Key, our team strives to provide a level of luxury that feels effortless and sincere, infusing wellness at every turn. The Southall team cares for our visitors with the same caliber of kindness and respect as we care for the humans that work alongside us.

Southall Farm and Inn is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Southall provides equal employment opportunities to applicants and employees and does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, transgender, national origin, status as a protected veteran, disability or any other classification protected by law. All aspects of employment including the decision to hire, promote, discipline, or discharge, will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs.

As Mercury continues its rapid growth trajectory, navigating an increasingly complex regulatory, partner, and product landscape is critical. Compliance is not only a requirement, but a competitive advantage that enables Mercury to move faster, build trust, and launch innovative products responsibly. 
Nowhere is that more true than in AI. We believe we have a path to lead the US banking* industry into the AI era, and that how we choose to build and deploy AI will define our success over the next three years. 
We are building first-party agentic products, headless and agent-accessible banking through our API and MCP, and the internal platforms that let us build with AI at speed. Core to all of it is great governance—these systems must run on one trusted system of access, logging, and data controls that meets the requirements of our banking ambitions.
We are seeking a Lead Compliance Risk Manager to serve as the compliance advisor for Mercury's AI products. This is a new, high-visibility role and the first dedicated compliance advisory seat covering AI at Mercury. You will be the leading authority on AI product compliance risk for the Compliance Team—shaping how we build, how we govern, and how we explain ourselves to our partners and regulators.
You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Legal, and Operations to ensure Mercury's AI products are compliant-by-design from concept through launch and scale. You will also help define the AI governance framework itself: the standards, controls, escalation paths, and documentation that allow a bank-partnered fintech to deploy agentic capabilities responsibly and at pace.
How this role fits alongside our other AI roles: this is a product compliance advisory role. Our Data & AI Governance team owns enterprise governance frameworks, responsible-AI standards, AI use case intake and inventory, and risk classification; Model Risk Management owns model inventory, tiering, and validation. You will be a close partner to and a major consumer of both—running our AI products through their processes, applying their standards to real product decisions, and bringing them the product-level detail they need to see. You will also help extend our existing product compliance playbooks to cover AI features, in partnership with your manager and the rest of the Product Compliance team. Your mandate is the products, not the program. 
In this role, you will:
Serve as the subject matter expert and primary compliance advisor for Mercury's AI and agentic products, including Command, our API, and agentic access methods such as MCP and CLI.
Work closely with cross-functional risk and product teams to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a way that meets all relevant financial partner, regulatory compliance obligations, and our AI governance standards.
Ensure all processes and products under your area of responsibility comply with applicable rules and regulations. Stay up to date with changes to applicable regulations, supervisory guidance, and emerging AI-specific law, and implement necessary updates to impacted products to maintain compliance.
Support expansion for new product launches by scoping, defining, and communicating product and compliance requirements.
Work cross-functionally to drive remediation efforts for products within your defined scope.
Support the compliance function in defining and achieving departmental initiatives, maintaining relevant policies and procedures, developing documentation solutions, and liaising with auditors.
Mentor and provide strategic guidance to compliance colleagues as AI capabilities spread across every product domain, and contribute to building a strong culture of compliance across Mercury.
Work closely with our Risk team, which owns AI governance, as Compliance’s AI product expert to contribute product-level guidance to ongoing AI governance updates.
Core responsibilities:
Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Operations, and Legal to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a manner that meets all relevant regulatory, financial partner, and network obligations.
Advise product and engineering teams throughout the product lifecycle—discovery, design, evaluation, launch, and iteration—to ensure AI products are compliant-by-design rather than reviewed after the fact.
Identify, assess, and document compliance risks specific to AI and agentic systems—including inaccurate or fabricated output, unauthorized or over-scoped agent action, inadequate consent and disclosure, unexplainable decisioning, disparate impact, data leakage across customers or organizations, prompt injection and third-party agent risk, and insufficient audit trail—and work cross-functionally to design pragmatic mitigation strategies.
Define the compliance requirements for the platforms AI is built on, in partnership with the teams that own them: the LLM gateway all internal traffic routes through, the internal app platform, agent orchestration frameworks, and the data access and governance layer.
Establish and refine AI-specific compliance standards for the department—what evidence a launch requires, what must be logged, what requires human review, what must be escalated, and what is out of bounds—and ensure those standards evolve as the organization and the technology grow.
Support new product launches and expansions by scoping, defining, and communicating compliance requirements clearly and early, including for co-marketing and distribution partnerships with third-party AI platforms.
Monitor regulatory, supervisory, and industry developments relevant to AI in financial services, assess impact, and drive implementation of required changes.
Own and oversee multiple concurrent high-impact AI compliance workstreams, holding project owners accountable for results and ensuring each aligns with department and company objectives.
Support remediation efforts for products within scope, including root cause analysis, corrective action planning, and execution tracking.
Partner with executive leadership, partner bank compliance teams, and external advisors to guide high-level decisions on AI direction, presenting data-driven recommendations.
Contribute to the broader Compliance function by supporting policy development, documentation standards, audit preparation, and examiner interactions.
Help build and reinforce a strong culture of compliance across Mercury through collaboration, education, and influence—including raising the AI fluency of the Compliance team itself, and developing scalable tools, templates, and frameworks others can reuse.
You should have:
8+ years of experience in a compliance advisory, product compliance, or regulatory risk role, ideally within fintech or financial services, with a track record of being the recognized authority in your domain.
Demonstrated experience advising on AI, machine learning, or model-driven products in a regulated environment—or comparable experience standing up a new compliance domain where no playbook existed.
Working knowledge of the regulatory and supervisory framework relevant to AI in banking, including UDAAP, fair lending and ECOA/Reg B, FCRA and adverse action, Reg E and payments authorization, BSA/AML, GLBA and privacy, marketing and disclosure requirements, recordkeeping, complaint management, model risk management expectations, and third-party and vendor risk management guidance.
Familiarity with emerging AI-specific regimes and frameworks and the ability to form a practical view on their application—such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, state AI and automated decisioning laws.
Technical fluency to engage credibly with engineers on model behavior, evaluation and testing, agent permissioning and tool scoping, logging and observability, and data access controls—and to know which questions actually surface risk.
Deep experience partnering with product and engineering teams on regulatory and compliance matters across the product lifecycle, including on fast-moving launches with external dependencies.
Proven ability to own highly ambiguous, large-scale compliance problems and to create and execute a strategy to address them, without waiting for precedent.
Experience designing compliance frameworks that span multiple product lines or departments, and improving systems and processes so that compliance posture evolves alongside business growth.
Demonstrated success operating with senior stakeholders, including executives, partner banks, auditors, or regulators, and presenting data-driven recommendations that drive decisions.
Strong project management skills, including the ability to define problems, create execution plans, manage several high-impact initiatives at once, and drive outcomes.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate regulatory and financial partner risk into terms stakeholder teams understand, and to resolve conflict around risk tolerance, resourcing, and timelines.
Experience mentoring mid-level compliance professionals and raising the capability of a team, not just delivering your own work.
Comfort operating independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment, with sound judgment on when to move and when to escalate.
Curiosity, adaptability, and genuine interest in engaging with frontier technology and the regulatory challenges that come with it.

title: Accountant
organization: Pacific Northwest University of Health Sciences
ai_core_responsibilities: The Accountant is responsible for general ledger accounting, account reconciliations, and maintaining fixed asset records to support the University's financial operations. They also assist with monthly and year-end close processes, financial reporting, and audit preparation while collaborating with various departments.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must possess a bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field. A minimum of two years of professional accounting experience is required, including proficiency in general ledger accounting and account reconciliations.
description_text:
Description
Recruitment Period: 10/06/2026 - Until Filled
Status: Full-Time, 40 hours/week
Salary Information: Annual Minimum Salary-$52,800-Annual Maximum Salary-$79,200
Hiring Rate: Dependent upon qualifications and experienceOn Campus Position
Pacific Northwest University of Health Sciences (PNWU) was founded as a 501(c) (3) non-profit medical institution in 2005 aimed at increasing access to health care in medically underserved areas of the Pacific Northwest.

The University currently offers the degrees of Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine, Doctor of Physical Therapy, Doctor of Dental Medicine, Master of Biomedical Sciences, and Master of Science in Occupational Therapy enrolling over 550 students annually. Interprofessional education partnerships with other universities adds another 100 students to the population. The campus includes 300 employees with academic programming spread over a five-state region.

PNWU is located in Yakima, WA, a city of approximately 95,000 located in the south-central part of the state near the eastern slopes of the Cascade Mountains in a major agricultural and outdoor recreation region. It is approximately 140 miles from Seattle, 170 miles from Portland, and 200 miles from Spokane. The Yakima Valley is a wonderful place to live, work and play. For more information, visit https://www.visityakima.com/.

Pacific Northwest University of Health Sciences (PNWU) does not sponsor employment visas. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and for the duration of their employment with PNWU. Employment eligibility will be verified in accordance with federal law.

General Summary:
The Accountant performs professional accounting work in support of the University’s financial operations and reporting. The position is responsible for general ledger accounting, account reconciliations, journal entries, fixed asset support, financial schedules, account research, and other recurring accounting activities.

The Accountant supports timely and accurate monthly and year-end close processes, maintains complete and well-supported financial records, and works collaboratively with Finance staff and University departments to research and resolve accounting matters.

The Accountant establishes credibility through consistent, accurate, and well-documented work; takes ownership of assigned responsibilities and follows through on deadlines; and builds positive working relationships across Finance and the University. The position approaches discrepancies with curiosity and sound judgment, welcomes feedback as a path to growth, and understands that careful stewardship of PNWU’s financial records supports the students and communities the University serves.

Essential Job Functions:

General Accounting and Monthly Close
Prepare recurring and non-recurring journal entries with appropriate supporting documentation.
Perform monthly reconciliations of assigned general ledger and balance sheet accounts and research and resolve discrepancies.
Maintain assigned account schedules and ensure transactions are accurately recorded, classified, and supported.
Participate in monthly and year-end close processes and complete assigned responsibilities within established deadlines.
Review assigned account activity for accuracy, completeness, and appropriate coding.
Research discrepancies, unusual transactions, and reconciling items and communicate unresolved or significant issues to the Controller.
Assist with accruals, allocations, prepaid expenses, and other recurring accounting activities.
Maintain organized and complete documentation supporting accounting transactions and reconciliations.
Cash and Balance Sheet Accounting
Prepare assigned bank, cash, and other balance sheet reconciliations. 
Research outstanding or unusual reconciling items and coordinate corrections as necessary.
Assist with recording and reconciliation of cash receipts, transfers, investment activity, and other cash-related transactions.
Support reconciliation between subsidiary systems and the general ledger.
Assist with maintaining schedules supporting receivables, liabilities, prepaid expenses, deposits, and other assigned balance sheet accounts.
Fixed Assets and Other Accounting Responsibilities
Maintain fixed asset records and supporting documentation for additions, disposals, transfers, and other asset activity. 
Assist with preparation and recording of depreciation and reconciliation of fixed asset records to the general ledger.
Review capital purchases for appropriate supporting documentation and classification under University capitalization policies.
Assist with accounting and reconciliation activities for leases, restricted funds, grants, capital projects, and other assigned areas.
Maintain recurring schedules and supporting documentation for assigned financial statement accounts.
Financial Reporting and Analysis
Assist with preparation of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports and supporting schedules.
Prepare recurring financial reports and account analyses as assigned.
Research account activity and assist with explanations of financial statement and budget variances.
Provide accurate actual financial information to support budgeting, forecasting, and other financial analysis.
Respond to routine accounting and transaction questions from University departments and assist with account research and coding, communicating clearly and patiently with non-financial colleagues.
Audit and Compliance
Prepare assigned schedules, reconciliations, workpapers, and supporting documentation for the annual financial statement audit and other audits or reviews.
Assist with responses to auditor requests and research supporting financial transactions as needed.
Maintain financial records and documentation in accordance with University policies, internal control requirements, and applicable record-retention standards.
Assist with financial information required for tax filings, regulatory reporting, and other external reporting.
Identify accounting errors, unusual transactions, or potential control concerns and communicate them promptly to the Controller.
Financial Systems and Process Improvement
Maintain proficiency in the University’s financial systems and related reporting tools.
Assist with testing and implementation of financial system upgrades, ERP changes, interfaces, and process improvements.
Identify opportunities to improve recurring accounting processes, reconciliations, documentation, and efficiency.
Assist with development and maintenance of written accounting procedures.
Support efforts to automate manual accounting processes while maintaining appropriate internal controls.
Finance Team Collaboration and Professional Practice
Work collaboratively with the Senior Accountant, Accounts Payable, Payroll, Student Accounts, Budget & Financial Planning, and other Finance functions.
Provide backup support for accounting and other Finance responsibilities as assigned and appropriately cross-trained, and assist Finance team members and University departments with account research and resolution of financial issues.
Participate in Finance projects, system implementations, and process-improvement initiatives.
Take initiative and ownership for assigned work, follow through on commitments, and communicate early when a deadline or result is at risk.
Build trusting working relationships across Finance and with University departments, clarifying expectations and roles before and during shared work and including the right people in the right conversations.
Resolve differences constructively and with care, listening to understand others’ perspectives and engaging in honest dialogue when there is disagreement.
Actively seek and apply feedback, regularly ask whether the work is being done right, and pursue continuous learning and technical growth relevant to current and future responsibilities.
Connect daily work to PNWU’s mission of serving rural and medically underserved communities, understanding how accurate, well-stewarded financial information supports students and the University.
Other duties as assigned
Understands and adheres to accreditation standards and expectations specific to the department.
Salary is commensurate with qualifications and experience. Pro-rated based on hours/week. For this role, our anticipated hiring range is $52,800-$79,200/annual)
Every range at PNWU divides into four quartiles anchored at the midpoint. Quartile placement blends what a person brings and how they perform, which is our commitment to behaviors and results expressed in placement mechanics. The general framework:
1st Quartile ($52,800-$59,400/annual). New to this level or role. Brings relevant experience but is new to the scope of work at this level; developing the full breadth of the role; generally 0 to 3 years at this level. Meets expectations and is still establishing a track record.
2nd Quartile ($59,400-$66,000/annual). Developing to proficient; generally 3 to 5 years at this level or equivalent. Proficient across core responsibilities, consistently meets and sometimes exceeds expectations, and has established credibility with colleagues and partners.
3rd Quartile ($66,000-$72,600/annual). Fully qualified and performing at market rate. The midpoint marks the fully qualified employee whose performance is satisfactory in all respects. Substantial experience, generally 5 to 10 years; consistently strong performance; serves as a trusted expert resource.
4th Quartile ($72,600-$79,200/annual). Highly skilled, consistently high-performing, high-contributing. Extensive experience, typically 10 or more years; recognized institutional expert whose work adds significant value. Reserved for the most senior and exceptional cases.
Requirements
Education
A bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field from an accredited institution. 
Experience:
Two years of professional accounting experience, including experience with general ledger accounting, account reconciliations, and journal entries.
An equivalent combination of education and experience that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to perform the essential functions of the position.
Desired Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities:
Working knowledge of accounting principles and practices, with strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Ability to identify discrepancies and research issues through resolution.
Integrity, accountability, and sound professional judgment.
Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to meet recurring deadlines and manage multiple priorities.
Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain accounting matters clearly to non-financial colleagues.
Proficiency with financial systems, spreadsheets, and related reporting tools.
Reliability, ownership, and follow-through, with a track record of delivering accurate work on recurring deadlines.
Ability to solve non-routine problems with curiosity and sound judgment, and to recognize when a matter should be escalated.
Ability to build trusting working relationships across Finance and with departments throughout the University.
Openness to feedback and a demonstrated commitment to continuous learning and professional growth.
Emotional intelligence and flexibility in navigating change, ambiguity, and differences in communication style and workstyle.
Ability to connect day-to-day financial work to PNWU’s mission and to the students and communities the University serves.
Commitment to internal controls, documentation, continuous improvement, and responsible stewardship of University resources.
To ensure full consideration submit:
A letter of introduction outlining background and qualifications for the position.
Detailed resume.
Contact information for three professional references.
The job announcement above is not the full job description but represents the job responsibilities and requirements. A full job description can be provided upon request.

title: Senior Director, FP&A
ai_core_responsibilities: The Senior Director will lead the company-wide FP&A function, overseeing budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning. They will serve as a strategic partner to executive leadership and global stakeholders to drive informed decision-making and resource allocation.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must possess a bachelor's degree and over 10 years of relevant finance experience, specifically within the biopharmaceutical industry. Strong financial acumen, leadership capabilities, and experience with enterprise-wide planning processes are essential.
description_text:
Company Description
Deciphera, a member of Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., is a biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing important new medicines and providing hope to people living with cancer, neurologic and autoimmune disease. Deciphera is leveraging its proprietary switch-control kinase inhibitor platform and deep expertise in kinase biology to develop a broad portfolio of innovative medicines. In addition to advancing multiple product candidates from Deciphera’s platform in clinical studies, QINLOCK® (ripretinib) is Deciphera’s switch-control kinase inhibitor approved in many countries including the European Union and the United States for the treatment of adult patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) who have received prior treatment with 3 or more kinase inhibitors, including imatinib. ROMVIMZA® (vimseltinib) is a kinase inhibitor approved in the United States for adult patients with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) for which surgical resection will potentially cause worsening functional limitation or severe morbidity, and in the European Union for adult patients with TGCT associated with clinically relevant physical function deterioration and in whom surgical options have been exhausted or would induce unacceptable morbidity or disability. 
The spirit of collaboration that has brought medications to life continues to guide how we operate, grow, and discover new breakthroughs. We cultivate an inclusive culture that values curiosity, creativity, and shared accountability—empowering individuals to challenge the unknown together. 
Deciphera offers competitive compensation, including equity-based compensation, and a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) retirement plan, life insurance and a flexible spending account for either health care and/or dependent care. 
Job Description
The Senior Director, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) will lead Deciphera’s FP&A function and serve as a key strategic and financial partner to executive leadership, functional leaders, and Ono Pharmaceutical’s corporate headquarters in Japan. This highly visible role is responsible for leading company-wide budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning while ensuring alignment between Deciphera’s business priorities and the broader Ono Pharma Group strategy.
The Senior Director will provide strategic financial leadership and analysis to support portfolio planning, investment decisions, and enterprise-wide resource allocation. Working closely with leaders across Deciphera and Ono Pharma headquarters, this individual will deliver financial insights, challenge key business assumptions, and help drive informed decision-making in support of both short- and long-term corporate objectives. In addition, the role will lead and develop a high-performing FP&A team while advancing the company’s financial planning, reporting, and decision-support capabilities to support continued growth and organizational success.
What You'll Do
Financial Planning & Analysis
Lead the company's annual budget and quarterly forecasting processes, establishing financial targets, key assumptions, and planning timelines.
Drive analysis of financial and operational performance against budget and forecast, identifying key drivers, risks, opportunities, and recommendations.
Partner with functional leaders throughout the organization to provide financial guidance, challenge assumptions, and support informed decision-making.
Lead financial reporting and forecasting activities in collaboration with Ono Pharmaceutical corporate headquarters.
Develop impactful financial analyses, business cases, and executive-level presentations for senior leadership and global stakeholders.
Ensure alignment between financial plans, strategic priorities, and operational objectives.
Enhance and streamline FP&A processes, tools, reporting capabilities, and planning methodologies.
Strategic Finance
Lead Deciphera's Strategic Finance function, providing direction and oversight on high-priority financial initiatives.
Partner cross-functionally to support portfolio strategy, investment decisions, resource allocation, and business planning.
Oversee financial modeling, scenario planning, and evaluation of strategic alternatives across development and commercial programs.
Translate complex financial analyses into clear, actionable insights for executive leadership and corporate stakeholders.
Team Leadership
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing finance team.
Establish clear goals, performance expectations, and career development plans.
Foster a culture of accountability, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and collaboration.
Build organizational capabilities that support Deciphera's growth and evolving business needs.
Other duties and responsibilities as assigned 
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
10+ years of relevant finance experience with significant FP&A and/or strategic finance leadership experience within the pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical industry.
Proven experience leading enterprise-wide budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning processes.
Strong financial and business acumen with demonstrated ability to influence strategic decisions through data-driven analysis.
Experience developing and presenting financial insights to executive leadership teams.
Demonstrated success leading, mentoring, and developing finance professionals.
Exceptional communication, presentation, collaboration, and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability to effectively partner with senior executives, cross-functional leaders, and global corporate stakeholders.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting portfolio planning, business development initiatives, and strategic investment decisions within the life sciences industry.
Experience operating within a global organization and collaborating with international stakeholders and corporate headquarters.
Advanced financial modeling, forecasting, and scenario-planning expertise.
Proven ability to build scalable FP&A processes and reporting capabilities in a growing organization.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment while balancing strategic leadership with hands-on execution.
Experience with enterprise planning and ERP systems; familiarity with Adaptive Insights and Oracle Fusion preferred.
Additional Information
Deciphera is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The base salary pay range for this role is $224,900- $309,200. Actual compensation packages will depend on various factors, including, but not limited to depth of experience, education, skillset, overall performance and/or location.​
Deciphera believes in providing a competitive compensation and benefits package to all employees. Our base salary is just one component of Deciphera’s competitive total rewards strategy that also includes annual performance bonus, a long-term incentive plan, full range of benefits and other incentive compensation plans (if applicable)
Benefits:
Competitive salary and annual bonus.
Comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision insurance, 401(k) retirement plan with company match, and more.
Generous parental leave and family planning benefits.
Outstanding culture and opportunities for personal and professional growth.
EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY INFORMATION
Deciphera is committed to equal employment opportunity and values diversity. To ensure that we comply with reporting requirements, we invite you complete the confidential survey at the end of this application. Providing this information is optional. It will not be accessible or used in the hiring process, and has no effect on your opportunity for employment. This information will also be treated confidentially. We are committed to make all hiring decisions and other employment decisions on a non-discriminatory basis.

ai_requirements_summary: A bachelor's degree in accounting or finance and at least 2 years of accounting experience are required. Proficiency in MS Office and experience with ERP or HRIS systems are essential, with preference given to candidates from the manufacturing or medical device industries.
description_text:
Description
Position Summary:
Supports multiple business entities by assuming responsibilities for accounts receivable/payable and general accounting. The incumbent analyzes, resolves, and recommends solutions to accounting variations and business issues. 

Job Duties and Responsibilities:
Prepares journal entries and account reconciliations ensuring accuracy of financial data.
Assists Controller with preparation of financial reports.
Generates and processes accounts receivable and accounts payable invoices daily and analyzes accuracy.
Records customer payments in a timely and accurate manner.
Monitors and takes appropriate action to collect past due invoices.
Creates a weekly AR Aging providing commentary to Controller.
Codes and enters invoices into accounting system ensuring appropriate expense allocation.
Maintains accounts payable invoice filing.
Coordinates accounts payable check run ensuring timely payments to vendors.
Executes core duties and responsibilities of the role in accordance with the established skills competencies. 
All other duties as assigned.


Requirements
Essential Skills and Experience:
Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance or related field of study, or equivalent combination of training and experience.
A minimum of 2 years of accounting experience is required. Experience in the manufacturing environment is preferred . Medical device manufacturing industry is preferred.
Proficient in understanding and interpretation of written and verbal instructions, directions, and technical information 
Intermediate computer competency in MS Office; Outlook, Excel, Word and ability to enter and maintain information needed within the HRIS and ERP systems is required. Knowledge of Paylocity HRIS, IQMS ERP, and QuickBooks is preferred.
Attention to detail: Demonstrates understanding the broader picture while maintaining focus on finer details.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including willingness to participate in cross-functional projects and teams.
Ability to act with integrity, professionalism, and confidentiality.
Reporting to this position: No direct reports.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:
The physical demands and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

title: Senior Accountant
ai_core_responsibilities: The Senior Accountant manages daily accounting operations, including month-end close, financial reporting, and general ledger integrity. They also oversee accounts receivable, cash operations, and ensure compliance with GAAP and relevant accounting standards.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance and at least 5 years of progressive accounting experience. Proficiency in GAAP, advanced Excel, and experience with NetSuite or similar accounting software is required.
description_text:
About Point
✨ Real Impact, Real People: Our mission at Point is to make homeownership more valuable and accessible. Your work directly helps homeowners access their wealth, achieve financial flexibility, and realize life changing goals.
✨ Funding: With over $175M raised from top investors like Andreessen Horowitz, WestCap, Greylock, and Prudential, we’re scaling fast! You have the opportunity to join us at a pivotal stage.
✨ Game-changing Product: We're building a category defining company in home equity. We’ve earned a 4.7 Trustpilot rating and an A+ from the BBB, a testament to the value we provide to our 20,000+ customers.
✨ Great Place to Work: Our employees love working here! We are a Certified Great Place to Work and a Fortune Best Workplaces in the Bay Area.
✨ Remote First Culture, Genuine Connection: Work from anywhere in the U.S. while staying closely connected through virtual collaboration, team gatherings, and a people-first culture. Select roles may require onsite work at our Palo Alto office one day per week.
Local or 100% Remote
About the role
The Senior Accountant oversees day-to-day accounting operations, including month-end close, financial reporting, and process improvement. This role safeguards general ledger integrity, reconciles balance sheet accounts, and supports timely, GAAP-compliant financial statements. The Senior Accountant also partners across teams on special projects, audit readiness, and scalable accounting workflows.
Your responsibilities
Perform core month-end close responsibilities including preparing/posting journal entries, reviewing G/L activity, and reconciling designated balance sheet accounts.
Manage accounts receivable: invoices, payment applications, and monitor aging. 
Partner with the manager to manage and refine complex revenue schedules. 
Manage daily cash operations, approving inter-account transfers and title company wire disbursements.
Monitor and manage the company and Investor cash positions.
Perform monthly bank reconciliations and daily cash reconciliations. 
Make recommendations to improve accounting department efficiency (workflows or software enhancements)
Prepare and support the preparation of monthly financial statements, consolidations, and multi-entity reporting
Ensure compliance with accounting standards including ASC 842 (leases) and ASC 606 (revenue recognition).
Analyze investor contracts to ensure custodial accounting requirements are met.
About you
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
5+ years of progressive accounting experience with strong general ledger ownership.
Solid understanding of GAAP and financial statement preparation.
Proven experience managing month-end close, journal entries, and balance sheet reconciliations.
Advanced Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookups, and reconciliation of large datasets.
Experience with NetSuite, FloQast (close management platform).Advanced Excel and Google Sheets skills
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment and manage multiple priorities to meet deadlines.
Experience supporting year-end audit and working with external auditors.
Experience in high-growth or small-team environments.
Compensation at Point will be determined by skills, experience, and geographic location. Point has identified the expected annual base salary for this role at this level based on the market by tiers (Region | Location | Market Salary):
Tier 1 | San Francisco Bay Area, New York, and Seattle | $114,000 - $126,000
Tier 2 | Austin, Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, Philadelphia, Portland, Sacramento, San Diego, Santa Barbara & Washington DC | $98,800 - $109,200
Tier 3 | All other US metro areas | $90,250 - $99,750
This does not include any other potential components of the compensation package, including equity, benefits, and perks outlined above. At the launch of each position, we benchmark compensation to the appropriate role and level utilizing competitive compensation data from various data sources as references. At the offer stage, we use the signal we received from our interviews, coupled with your experience, location, and other job-related factors, to determine final compensation.
Location Requirement: This is a remote position. However, candidates must reside in one of Point’s states of operation: AL, AR, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, IL, KS, KY, MA, MD, ME, MI, MN, MO, NC, NH, NJ, NV, NY, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI.
Our benefits
Generous health benefits: We provide comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans with options for flexible spending accounts (FSA) and health savings accounts (HSA).
Unlimited paid time off: Recharge with unlimited paid time off and 10 company holidays.
Flexible remote and onsite work: Our teams work from many different locations and time zones. We support fully remote work and also have an amazing in-person environment in our downtown Palo Alto, CA HQ.
Fully paid parental leave: Point will supplement state Paid Family Leave (PFL) so employees receive 100% of their regular base pay, plus two additional weeks of fully paid leave after state PFL ends. In states without PFL, Point offers up to 8 weeks of paid parental leave. In addition, employees also receive 4 weeks of fully paid transition time, during which you may work 2–3 days per week while receiving full base pay.
Equity: We offer meaningful equity because we believe in sharing the value you help create. Your contributions directly impact our growth, and your equity gives you a stake in our future success.
Financial wellness: We provide 401K retirement plans for employees as well as guaranteed life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage.
Extra work/life benefits: We provide monthly stipends for internet, mobile plans, wellness perks, a one-time home office reimbursement, and company provided equipment including a MacBook and monitor.
Point is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We provide employment opportunities regardless of age, race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other protected class. Each individual at Point brings their own perspectives, work experiences, lifestyles, and cultures with them, and we believe that a more diverse team creates more innovative products, provides better services to customers, and helps us all grow and learn.

description_text:
BOOKKEEPING CONTRACTOR


JOB DESCRIPTION & SCOPE OF WORK

Department: Finance
Reports To: Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
Position Type: Part-Time Independent Contractor
Contract Rate: $28.85 per hour
Estimated Hours: 20 hours per week
Anticipated Start Date: As Soon As Possible
Contract Duration: Ongoing

About Asian Americans Advancing Justice-Atlanta

Our mission is to advance justice in a broad multiracial movement and build power within Asian Americans, Pacific Islanders (AAPI) Arab, Middle Eastern, Muslim, and South Asian (AMEMSA), and immigrant communities across Georgia and the Southeast. We envision a just world that embraces self-determination, transformative solidarity, and thriving communities.

 

Founded in 2010 as the Asian American Legal Advocacy Center (AALAC), our organization became part of the Asian Americans Advancing Justice affiliation in 2014. Since then, we have re-organized our focus areas more specifically into four groups: Policy Advocacy [https://www.advancingjustice-atlanta.org/policy-advocacy], Civic Engagement [https://www.advancingjustice-atlanta.org/organizing-civic-engagement] & Organizing, Impact Litigation [https://www.advancingjustice-atlanta.org/impact-litigation], and Legal Services [https://www.advancingjustice-atlanta.org/legal-services].

 

About The (Department)

The finance department is responsible for managing the company's overall finances and supporting the other departments including, but not limited to, procuring and  vendor payment, tracking cash flow, expenditure, investments, financial planning and analyzing business trends. The finance department decides how much funds are needed and when, how best to use the available funds

Position Summary

We are seeking a detail-oriented and dependable Accounting Contractor to provide essential accounting and financial administrative support to the Finance Department. This individual will assist with day-to-day accounting operations, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, cash flow tracking, account reconciliations, financial recordkeeping, and payroll support.

The ideal contractor will possess strong organizational skills, accuracy in financial data management, and the ability to manage multiple accounting priorities while maintaining confidentiality and compliance with established financial policies and procedures.

The Accounting Contractor will work with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to ensure timely processing of financial transactions, accurate record keeping, and the overall efficiency of the Finance Department.


SCOPE OF WORK & KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

How You’ll Contribute to Our Impact


ACCOUNTS PAYABLE & VENDOR MANAGEMENT

 * Process accounts payable transactions and coordinate timely vendor payments.

 * Review invoices for accuracy, appropriate documentation, and required approvals before processing payments.

 * Obtain and maintain vendor W-9 forms, payment information, and supporting documentation.

 * Track outstanding invoices and payment obligations.

 * Process and maintain records of employee reimbursements.

 * Investigate and resolve vendor payment discrepancies as needed.


 ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE & CASH FLOW MANAGEMENT

 * Support accounts receivable activities, including recording and tracking incoming payments.

 * Monitor and maintain cash flow records and assist with tracking balances.

 * Record donations and other financial transactions.


 GENERAL ACCOUNTING & RECONCILIATION

 * Enter and maintain accurate financial data into quickbooks.

 * Prepare and post journal entries and update financial records as directed.

 * Verify, record, and reconcile organizational credit card transactions.

 * Investigate questionable transactions, discrepancies, or incomplete financial data and recommend appropriate corrective actions.

 * Ensure financial records are organized, accurate, and supported by appropriate documentation.


 PAYROLL & TIMESHEET SUPPORT

 * Review and input  timesheets into TriNet.

 * Serve as a backup for designated payroll processing responsibilities, as needed.

 * Assist with verifying payroll-related information and resolving discrepancies.


 FINANCIAL REPORTING & ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT

 * Compile financial data and prepare routine and ad hoc reports as requested by the CFO.

 * Maintain organized electronic accounting records, spreadsheets, and supporting documentation.

 * Provide general accounting and administrative assistance to support the daily operations of the Finance Department.

 * Communicate financial discrepancies, outstanding items, and potential concerns to the CFO in a timely manner.

 * Assist with additional finance-related projects and assignments as deemed necessary by the CFO.

What You’ll Bring 

 * Minimum of 1–2 years of relevant accounting, bookkeeping, or financial administrative experience.

 * Experience using QuickBooks or similar accounting software.

 * Prior accounting or financial administrative experience within a nonprofit organization.

 * Working knowledge of general accounting principles and practices.

 * Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Outlook, and Word.

 * Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to maintain accurate financial records.

 * Ability to prioritize assignments, manage deadlines, and work independently.

 * Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality when handling sensitive financial and organizational information.

 * Effective communication and problem-solving skills.

To Apply  

Submit a resume and cover letter to Human Resources through the job link. Applications will be accepted and considered until the contract is filled. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States.

This Scope of Work outlines the anticipated services and expectations of the engagement. Final terms, including contract duration, invoicing procedures, payment schedule, confidentiality, and termination provisions, will be established in the independent contractor agreement.

Asian Americans Advancing Justice-Atlanta is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified persons are encouraged to apply, regardless of race, color, creed, ethnicity, national origin, ancestry, age, height, weight, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, HIV status, marital or domestic partner status, or religious affiliation. For any accommodation requests in the application process, please contact hr@advancingjustice-atlanta.org

Harbor-Hickam), requires a CAC, and a favorable Tier 1/NACI-SF85 background

monitoring budget execution, processing funding documents, supporting

quarterly targets, and 80/20 rule compliance.

reports.

Reports.

• Review work tasks and validate costs for reimbursable activities.

description_text:
At Qualia, we've built the leading B2B real estate technology that transforms the home buying and selling experience into a simple, secure, and enjoyable process. Our SMB and Enterprise products bring together users from across the real estate ecosystem---homebuyers and sellers, lenders, title and escrow agents, and real estate agents---onto a single shared digital closing platform, providing greater clarity and transparency to real estate transactions. Today, through our business customers across the country, millions of consumers use Qualia to close on homes every year.
WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON
Qualia's billing environment is complex. We manage subscription billing, usage-based charges, marketplace transactions, multiple credit structures, and a wide range of payment terms across thousands of customers. This role sits at the center of it all. As a Billing Specialist on the Revenue Operations team, you'll own and run core billing operations — processing payments, resolving billing discrepancies, generating invoices, managing credits, and ensuring our customers are billed accurately and on time. You'll work closely with Deal Desk, Finance, Customer Success, Growth Management, and Engineering to maintain data integrity across the full quote-to-cash lifecycle. This is not a back-office role. You are the point person for billing-related questions from customer-facing teams, and the quality of your work directly impacts customer trust, revenue recognition, and Qualia's ability to grow.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Day-to-day billing operations: Oversee the billing status of accounts by researching and resolving billing inconsistencies, errors, and edge cases. Process incoming payments, manage billing runs, and ensure invoices are generated accurately — including for customers on non-standard payment plans, split payments, and deferred terms
Invoicing and customer billing materials: Create invoices and custom billing materials for Strategic and High Growth accounts. Review customer payment plans regularly for timely payments and follow up where necessary
Credits and adjustments: Manage the application of bank partner credits, ORT credits, and Qualia credits to customer accounts. Investigate and resolve situations where credits have not been applied correctly, and ensure visibility for customer-facing teams into credit balances and application history
Refunds and concessions: Manage the approval process for concessions and refunds. Issue refunds, collect on failed charges, and review payment disputes in accordance with established approval thresholds
Collections and past-due account management: Own the collections process for overdue accounts, including direct outreach to customers via email and phone. Navigate sensitive payment conversations with professionalism and empathy, working to resolve outstanding balances while preserving strong customer relationships and escalating to Growth Management or Customer Success when needed
Cross-functional collaboration: Serve as the primary point of contact for billing-related support cases from Growth Managers, Customer Success Managers, and Support. Participate in daily billing standups and biweekly case reviews to identify patterns, reduce repeat inquiries, and surface systemic issues
Data quality: Monitor billing data for errors such as duplicate subscriptions, incorrect plan amounts, overstated allotments, and misconfigured charges. Proactively flag issues before they reach customers rather than waiting for inbound reports
YOUR BACKGROUND THAT LIKELY MAKES YOU A MATCH
1–2 years of experience in billing operations, accounts receivable, or a revenue operations role — ideally in a SaaS or subscription-based environment
Experience with subscription billing platforms (Ordway, Zuora, Chargebee, or similar) and familiarity with how billing systems integrate with CRMs and ERPs
Strong command of Excel and Google Sheets; comfortable working with large datasets to investigate discrepancies and build reports
High attention to detail and a low tolerance for unresolved loose ends — you follow issues through to completion
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to explain complex billing situations clearly to both internal teams and customers
Ability to work well with ambiguity, prioritize across competing requests, and problem-solve independently in a fast-paced environment
Comfort navigating cross-functional relationships — you'll work daily with Deal Desk, Finance, Engineering, and customer-facing teams
Nice to Have:
Experience with Salesforce, Intacct, Ordway, or Stripe
Familiarity with revenue recognition concepts (ASC 606) and how billing data feeds into accounting processes
Experience with collections or dunning processes
Background in real estate, fintech, or title & escrow
Based in Austin, TX, with the ability to work in the office a minimum of two days per week is required. 
WHY QUALIA
Qualia is made up of incredibly bright, mission-driven coworkers who are passionate about using technology to solve real-world problems---and we're growing quickly. In order to continue building an engaging and dynamic organization, we're committed to giving everyone the support they need to do great work.
Our benefits package is designed to allow our team members to be their best selves, both in and out of the workplace. In addition to comprehensive health plans, a 401k program, and commuter benefits, we prioritize family and personal well-being through professional development, parental leave, and a flexible time off policy. Qualia offers a robust online onboarding program to train new hires, biweekly all hands meetings, and a variety of internal virtual events to keep employees connected.
We believe diverse perspectives and backgrounds are critical to building great technology, and our goal is to cultivate an environment where people feel equally valued and respected. Qualia is proud to be an equal-opportunity workplace, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital status, age, citizenship, socioeconomic status, disability, or veteran status.
By submitting your application, you acknowledge and agree to the collection, processing, and use of your personal information as described in our Employee Data Privacy Notice.

Individual applicants residing in the US only

About the role
As a Senior Onboarding Accounting Specialist, you'll be the first point of contact for new Uplinq clients — guiding them through system setup, data clean-up, and account activation. 
This is a high-touch, high-volume role: you'll juggle a large, active portfolio of clients at different onboarding stages, which means the job rewards people who communicate early and often, adapt quickly when something isn't working, and hold themselves accountable for outcomes rather than just effort.
The right candidate will have a magnetic presence on calls and an excitement about interaction with small business owners. The ideal candidate is a person the clients look forward to speaking with, someone who makes them feel confident in the investment they’ve made when choosing Uplinq. 

What you'll do
Lead daily client meetings to gather financial data, clarify scope, and build trust from the first call — earning it through rapport, clarity, and follow-through, not just technical accuracy.
Set up and configure Uplinq and QuickBooks Online accounts, including resolving integration and access issues (Plaid connections, payroll, revenue processors, inventory systems, etc) so systems sync cleanly from day one.
Compare signed proposals to actual client needs in the first call, and flag scope or pricing mismatches immediately — to sales, to your manager, and directly to the client — rather than letting a gap surface later and erode trust.
Manage a high volume of onboarding timelines and deliverables simultaneously, and proactively speak up when your workload or a specific account is at risk of falling behind, so it can be addressed before it becomes a bigger problem.
Troubleshoot setup and data issues using sound accounting judgment, and treat mistakes as fast information rather than something to hide — surface them quickly, learn from them, and adjust.
Find workarounds to keep stalled onboardings moving — manual data entry when a feed breaks, alternate document paths, creative scheduling — because an on-time, good-enough solution beats a stalled account waiting for a perfect one.
Collaborate with Sales, Initialization, Accounting, and Tax teams to resolve handoff gaps, own your part of the process end-to-end, and transition accounts smoothly into ongoing support.

Qualifications
6+ years in a client-facing accounting or onboarding role, ideally in public or multi-client accounting firm as Senior Associate level or higher
6+ years of daily QuickBooks use including Online setup, integrations, and troubleshooting (not desktop).
Strong working knowledge of both cash- and accrual-based accounting.
Demonstrated ability to manage 25+ active client relationships at once without letting communication or follow-through slip — someone who escalates early, adapts on the fly, and takes ownership of outcomes rather than absorbing pressure silently.
A warm, confident, and memorable presence with clients — someone who builds real rapport fast, puts anxious business owners at ease, and makes a technical process feel personal rather than transactional. 
Comfortable having direct conversations with clients about scope and pricing when what they signed doesn't match what they need, and willing to admit and correct course quickly when something's off.

Why Join Us
Competitive pay + health, dental, vision, 401(k), and life insurance
Remote-first and flexible work culture
Clear path for career growth in a fast-growing firm
Modern tech stack and automation-first mindset
Supportive, collaborative team with strong systems and documentation

description_text:
Job Summary:

Our Business Incentives Group (“BIG”) business has doubled in the last three
years and tripled in the last six. BIG Experienced Associates have been key to
our success, and they are central to our plans to continue as one of BDO’s
premiere national consulting practices.

As a Tax Experienced Associate, Business Incentives Group, you will help achieve
BDO’s core purpose—helping people thrive every day—by helping companies and
individuals identify and claim government incentives designed to promote
innovation and economic and job growth in the U.S. Like the BIG Tax Credit.

Our clients are leaders in innovation in virtually every industry, from
technology, manufacturing, life sciences, and healthcare to retail, consumer
products, and natural resources. As a Tax Experienced Associate, you will have
the opportunity and charge to innovate as well, collaborating with BDOers in all
of our business lines as well as with our clients’ innovation leaders, in tax,
accounting, and finance, and also in their BIG, engineering, software,
manufacturing, scientific, medical, and other BIG-related departments. 

BIG’s short-term mission is to help our clients as efficiently and effectively
as possible identify, document, and support on examination by tax authorities
all of the BIG-related incentives to which they are legally entitled. Our
longer-term goal is to develop an understanding of them as people and of all
aspects of their business so that we are well positioned as their trusted
advisors, as professionals who understand both their business operations and
business drivers as well as how BDO can help them realize their goals. 

In pursuing this mission, we are also seeking to help our Tax Experienced
Associates, Business Incentives Group become trusted advisors, ensuring they
have a clear sense of the importance and responsibilities of such a role, as
well as the training and opportunities to fill it. 

Toward that end, Tax Experienced Associates pursue opportunities to enable them
to gain and improve their skills in every aspect of professional service,
including technical, interpersonal, oral and written communication, project
management, practice management, and business development.

Job Duties:

 * Proactively assists in the execution of multiple client engagements
 * Collaborates with other BIGers in all aspects of our business, e.g.,
   innovating; developing and implementing better strategies and processes for
   our services, marketing, etc.
 * Establishes effective working relationships directly with BIGers and our
   clients, internal—other BDOers—and external
 * Contributes to the development of personal and to BIG’s technical acumen and
   market prominence
 * Keeps up to date with local and national business and economic issues
 *  Actively participates in business development activities to further develop
   your own professional network, with BDOers and others, and identifies and
   researches opportunities for new and existing clients 
 * Contributes to, supports, and enhances the culture of BIG, our local offices,
   and BDO as a globally leading professional services firm
 * Other duties as required

 

Supervisory Responsibilities:

 * N/A

 

Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Experience:

 * One (1) or more years of prior related experience, required 

     License/Certifications:

 * N/A

Software:

 * Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office Suite, specifically Microsoft Word
   and advanced level skillset in Microsoft Excel, preferred

Language:

 * N/A

Other Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

 * Excellent verbal and written communication skills 
 * Ability to interact effectively with people at all organizational levels of
   the firm 
 * Ability to work independently within a team environment and with a customer
   service focus 
 * Superior organizational skills and project management skills required with
   ability to multi-task in a fast- paced, deadline-driven environment
 * Strong initiative and drive to lead while seeking opportunities to enhance
   and grow the BIG practice

title: Compliance Specialist Multi-Property - Full Time
ai_core_responsibilities: The Compliance Specialist is responsible for enforcing federal reporting requirements, including the Bank Secrecy Act and Title 31, to minimize regulatory risk. They also conduct internal audits, investigate suspicious activities, and provide training to team members to ensure property-wide compliance.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates should have at least three years of experience in an administrative or auditing role, with a bachelor's degree in a business-related field preferred. Strong knowledge of federal gaming regulations and the ability to obtain a gaming license in multiple jurisdictions are required.
description_text:
WE’RE CHANGING ENTERTAINMENT. COME JOIN US.
We’re always looking for talent that believes in having fun. At PENN Entertainment, you’ll get to be a part of an exciting industry, where the days and nights are fast paced. You’ll work with an incredibly diverse set of coworkers driven by their enthusiasm for helping people find and have more fun. You’ll also get to work at a company that cares about your career growth and will help you get the support you need to expand your possibilities.
Initial placement within the salary range is based on an individual's relevant knowledge, skills, and experience. Base salary is just one component of our competitive Total Rewards package, which includes wellness programs designed to support our team members' financial, physical, and mental well-being. Specific benefits—such as day-one medical coverage, 401(k) matching, and annual performance bonus—may vary by position. Paid time off is earned according to the local policy and increases with the length of employment.
Click HERE to discover how we empower team members to grow, thrive, and advance in their careers.
WE LOVE OUR WORK.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES
(These functions are intended as a general illustration of the work performed in this job classification and are not all inclusive for this position)
Delivers superior internal and external guest service the Penn Entertainment Inc. way by ensuring every interaction includes our Service Standards and work harmoniously with fellow team members.
Daily interpretations and enforcements of federally mandated reporting requirements of the Code of Federal Regulations (Bank Secrecy Act) and Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN).
Minimizes regulatory risk of IRS fines and penalties by maintaining the Title 31 Compliance program so as to ensure the highest level of team member awareness, accurate capturing of currency transactions, effective daily audits of all Title 31 paperwork, and timely filing of all Currency Transaction Reports (CTR) and Suspicious Activity Reports (SAR) to the IRS and FinCEN, respectively, as required by federal law.
Trains team members, as needed, to ensure thorough knowledge and complete comprehension of federal Title 31 regulations and supplemental property and departmental procedures developed to meet these requirements. Conducts discretionary team member assessments by analyzing Title 31 test scores, exception reports, patterned discrepancies, and accuracy of form completion, recognizing areas of exposure with regard to Title 31 and subsequently providing recommended action to the Director of Compliance. 
Continual development and improvement of the property’s Title 31 Compliance Program, to include on-going evaluation of departmental procedures, training materials, and system capabilities of capturing cash-in and cash-out transactions.
Ability to work independently and objectively while exhibiting sound discretion when researching and interpreting federal requirements, educating team members, scrutinizing data, and/or seeking resolution of Title 31 issues.
Ability to thoroughly investigate suspicious activities ensuring the most complete and detailed narrative of events are reported in a timely manner to FinCEN via the Suspicious Activity Report, as well as, demonstrating sound judgment when determining appropriate action(s) necessary with regard to potential guests account status which may include the designation of Gaming Prohibited.
Conducts routine assessments of the property’s Responsible Gaming efforts to ensure compliance with Corporate standards, the American Gaming Associations, and the New Mexico and Nevada Gaming Control Boards standards and Code of Conduct, reporting any identified failures to the Director of Compliance.
Provides assistance with compliance related investigations and audits as assigned by the Director of Compliance.
Manages the administrative maintenance associated with self-ban/trespass guest accounts within the casino management system and report to the Director of Compliance any discrepancies noted.
Performs responsibilities independently, with little supervision while maintaining the ability to make informed and educated decisions.
Queries, audits and maintains custom computer reports, spreadsheets and word documents files.
Performs data entry and utilize scanning software.
Maintains and organizes department files as directed.
Completes special projects as assigned by the Director of Compliance and recommends improvement and/or corrective actions as necessary.
Maintains a positive attitude at all times, supporting the policies of Senior Management.
Maintains strict confidentiality regarding all matters related to M Resort and Zia Park compliance department including areas governed by Penn Entertainment, Inc. Compliance Program.
Adheres to guest service requirement listed above.
Adheres to, interpret, support, and explain established company policies and procedures as well as applicable local, state, federal and other regulatory procedures.
Fosters and maintains positive team member relations in a supportive environment and interfaces with other departments to ensure a harmonious working relationship.
Continue professional development of self.
Maintains a high level of professional appearance, demeanor, ethics, and image of self.
Conducts and attends all regular departmental meetings as well as other related meetings.
Completes necessary reports in a timely manner to meet deadlines.
Must be able to work flexible hours including evenings, weekends, and holidays.
Perform related duties as assigned.
BRING US YOUR BEST.
EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:
(Related education and experience may be interchangeable on a year for year basis)
Three (3) years experience in preferably an administrative or auditing position.
Bachelor’s degree with emphasis in management, business, finance OR an equivalent combination of education and experience preferred.
Knowledge of Title 31 and the Bank Secrecy Act preferred.
Strong problem solving, mediation, coaching, and consulting skills.
Excellent verbal and written communications skills.
Excellent interpersonal skills
Knowledgeable of applicable federal, state, and local regulations.
Fully Competent in Microsoft Office
Knowledge of Internet and database search capabilities
Ability to sustain a high level of confidentiality and professionalism.
Ability to maintain a high level of energy and take a proactive and strategic approach to dealing with issues.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively and communicate effectively with team members at all levels of the organizations.
Uses diplomacy and tact to build constructive and effective relationships including during high-tension situations.
Ability to obtain support for ideas and actions from subordinates, peers, or superiors in order to accomplish a task or goal. 
Highly organized and detail oriented.
Uses time efficiently and effectively to manage priorities.
Deals with simple and complex concepts effectively.
Ability to identify circumstances or incidents that require the notification and/or approval of others. 
Ability to administer training classes to groups and individuals.
Ability to review documents for regulatory requirements.
Knowledge and ability to interpret the BSA’s Title 31 reporting requirements.
Knowledge and ability to interpret NMGCB and NVGCB Regulations and Statutes.
Ability to perform research of regulatory matters both federal and state
Must successfully pass background check
Must obtain Gaming License in multiple jurisdictions
Must be 21 years of age
STAY IN THE GAME. FOLLOW US.
We’ve grown to become the leading provider of integrated entertainment, sports content, and casino gaming experiences thanks to our 43 destinations across North America, online sports betting and iCasino via theScore Bet Sportsbook and Casino®.
Being an industry leader means more than being a purveyor of fun. We are also committed to values like diversity and sustainability — for our community, our team members, our vendors, and our planet. 
We're changing entertainment. Follow us.
Equal Opportunity Employer

Apply today and grow with us.
