description_text:
Overview
Are you curious, detail-oriented, and eager to build a career in public accounting? Whether you're graduating soon or have a year or two of experience and are ready for a new opportunity, we'd love to meet you.
As a Staff Auditor, you'll work alongside experienced professionals serving clients across a variety of industries, including Healthcare, Not-for-Profit, Financial Services, Manufacturing, Construction, Higher Education, and more. You'll gain hands-on experience, build meaningful client relationships, and develop the technical and professional skills needed for long-term success in audit and assurance.
From day one, you'll be supported by a team that is invested in your growth. Through coaching, mentoring, structured training, and real-world client experience, you'll strengthen your analytical thinking, communication, problem-solving, and leadership skills while building a strong foundation in public accounting.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys learning, asking questions, collaborating with others, and tackling new challenges. As your experience grows, you'll take on increasing responsibility, greater client interaction, more complex engagements, and opportunities to develop specialized expertise.
We encourage participation in professional and community activities and are committed to supporting your pursuit of the CPA and other professional credentials.
Why You'll Thrive Here
Work alongside experienced professionals who are committed to your development.
Receive hands-on coaching and mentorship early in your career.
Gain exposure to multiple industries and business environments.
Build both technical accounting knowledge and professional skills.
Take on increasing responsibility as your confidence and experience grow.
Access robust learning and development resources, including CPA support.
Join a collaborative, people-focused culture that values curiosity, teamwork, and continuous learning.
Travel Expectations: This role requires minimal travel, less than 10% per year. Travel to client sites can range up to 50%.
You Will
Participate in audit, review, and compilation engagements for a diverse portfolio of clients.
Develop an understanding of client operations, financial reporting processes, and industry-specific risks.
Assist in preparing workpapers, audit documentation, and financial statements.
Analyze financial information, identify inconsistencies, and ask thoughtful questions to deepen your understanding.
Collaborate with team members and clients to gather information and support engagement objectives.
Build strong communication skills through regular interactions with colleagues, managers, and clients.
Develop proficiency in accounting, audit, and technology tools used throughout the firm.
Apply feedback from supervisors and mentors to continuously improve your technical and professional skills.
Manage multiple priorities and deadlines while maintaining attention to detail and quality.
Progress toward CPA certification and other professional development goals.
You Have
Bachelor's degree in Accounting or expected completion prior to start date. Master's degree is a plus but not required.
Internship, co-op, campus leadership, customer service, or other professional experience is helpful but not required.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Curiosity and a desire to understand how businesses operate.
Critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
Attention to detail and a commitment to producing quality work.
Strong organizational and time-management skills.
A willingness to seek feedback, learn from others, and continuously improve.
Ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment.
Basic proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
Interest in pursuing CPA licensure.
Compensation Details

ai_requirements_summary: Requires a bachelor's degree or higher and 15+ years of relevant experience in Internal Audit, Technology Risk, or Engineering Governance within financial services. description_text:
The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. is a leading global investment banking, securities
and investment management firm that provides a wide range of financial services
to a substantial and diversified client base that includes corporations,
financial institutions, governments, and individuals. Founded in 1869, the firm
is headquartered in New York and maintains offices in all major financial
centers around the world. We commit people, capital and ideas to help our
clients, shareholders and the communities we serve to grow. Our people are our
greatest asset – we say it often and with good reason. It is only with the
determination and dedication of our people that we can serve our clients,
generate long-term value for our shareholders and contribute to the broader
public. We take pride in supporting each colleague both professionally and
personally. From collaborative workspaces and ergonomic services to wellbeing
and resilience offerings, we offer our people the flexibility and support they
need to reach their goals in and outside the office

 

INTERNAL AUDIT

In Internal Audit, we ensure that Goldman Sachs maintains effective controls by
assessing the reliability of financial reports, monitoring the firm’s compliance
with laws and regulations, and advising management on developing smart control
solutions. Our group has unique insight on the financial industry and its
products and operations. We’re looking for detail-oriented team players who have
an interest in financial markets and want to gain insight into the firm’s
operations and control processes.

 

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

Goldman Sachs Internal Auditors demonstrate strong risk and control mindsets,
analytical, exercise professional skepticism and are able to challenge and
discuss effectively with management on risks and control measures.  We look for
individuals who enjoy learning about audit, businesses and functions, have
innovative and creative mindsets to adopt analytical techniques to enhance audit
techniques, building relationships and are able to evolve and thrive in teamwork
and in a fast-paced global environment.

 

YOUR IMPACT

As the third line of defense, Internal Audit’s mission is to independently
assess the firm’s internal control structure, including the firm’s governance
processes and controls, and risk management and capital and anti-financial crime
frameworks, raise awareness of control risk and monitor the implementation of
management’s control measures. In doing so, internal Audit:

 

 * Communicates and reports on the effectiveness of the firm’s governance, risk
   management and controls that mitigate current and evolving risk

 * Raise awareness of control risk

 * Assesses the firm’s control culture and conduct risks

 * Monitors management’s implementation of control measures

 

Goldman Sachs Internal Audit comprises individuals from diverse backgrounds
including chartered accountants, developers, risk management professionals,
cybersecurity professionals, and data scientists. We are organized into global
teams comprising business and technology auditors to cover all the firm’s
businesses and functions, including securities, investment banking, consumer and
investment management, risk management, finance, cyber-security and technology
risk, and engineering.

 

RESPONSIBILITIES

 * Lead Internal Audit coverage of the Global Banking & Markets (GBM) Public
   Equities Engineering environment, maintaining a deep understanding of
   business strategy, technology architecture, regulatory developments, and
   emerging risks to inform audit coverage and continuous monitoring activities.

 * Direct the planning and execution of complex audit engagements, including
   risk assessments, scoping, control evaluation, testing, reporting, and issue
   validation, ensuring high-quality and risk-focused audit outcomes.

 * Evaluate the design and effectiveness of controls across trading platforms,
   Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) processes, change management, cloud
   environments, operational resilience, and other critical technology and
   engineering functions.

 * Build strong relationships with senior Engineering, business, and control
   stakeholders, providing independent challenge and communicating audit
   conclusions, control weaknesses, and thematic risk observations to senior
   management.

 * Lead, coach, and develop audit professionals while advancing Internal Audit
   initiatives related to data analytics, automation, continuous monitoring, and
   audit methodology enhancement.

SKILLS AND RELEVANT EXPERIENCE

 * Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Engineering, Information
   Systems, Information Security, Finance, Accounting, or a related discipline.

 * 15+ years of relevant experience in Internal Audit, Technology Audit,
   Technology Risk, Operational Risk, Controls, Compliance, or Engineering
   Governance within financial services.

 * Significant experience auditing or assessing risks and controls within
   Equities, Equity Derivatives, Prime Brokerage, Securities Lending, Electronic
   Trading, or other capital markets businesses.

 * Demonstrated experience leading complex audits and managing geographically
   distributed teams.

 * Strong understanding of financial markets, trading workflows, and the
   technology platforms that support front-to-back business processes.

 * Experience interacting with and challenging senior Engineering and business
   leaders in a high-visibility environment.

 * Strong analytical, problem-solving, and risk assessment capabilities with the
   ability to evaluate complex technology and control environments.

 * Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience
   presenting audit conclusions and risk themes to senior management.

 * Relevant professional certifications preferred, including CISA, CIA, CISSP,
   CRISC, CISM, CPA, CFA, or equivalent credentials.

title: Credit Risk Analyst - GM Financial Bank
ai_core_responsibilities: The Credit Risk Analyst supports the AVP of Credit Risk by monitoring credit strategies, analyzing portfolio performance, and creating reports for management. They also assist in maintaining credit policies and ensuring data accuracy within a startup banking environment.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a bachelor's degree in a quantitative field and 0-2 years of experience in data analysis or portfolio reporting. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with large datasets are required, while familiarity with SQL, SAS, or Power BI is preferred.
description_text:
Why GM Financial Bank?

GM Financial Bank is a newly formed bank. Team members joining now will play a
pivotal role in shaping the bank, which will offer auto finance and deposit
products. Joining GM Financial Bank means an opportunity to help build a
customer-focused bank from the ground up.

This position will be posted until filled.


RESPONSIBILITIES

About the role:

The Credit Risk Analyst supports the AVP – Credit Risk in managing, monitoring
and reporting on credit risk strategies. The position provides analytical
insight into credit performance, policy execution and portfolio trends while
developing a foundational understanding of consumer credit, underwriting
practices and bank regulatory expectations. The position will work with a
variety of internal clients as well as interacting with Management. This role
offers a strong development opportunity for an analytically driven early-career
professional through structured coaching and exposure to leadership and credit
governance.

In this role you will:

 * Operate effectively in a startup banking environment, demonstrating the
   agility to manage multiple priorities, adapt quickly to changing needs, and
   assume new responsibilities as the credit program continues to evolve
 * Support the AVP – Credit Risk in the development, monitoring and reporting of
   credit risk strategies
 * Create recurring and ad-hoc credit risk reports, dashboards and analysis for
   management and governance committees
 * Analyze origination trends, portfolio performance and credit execution
   metrics to identify emerging risks and opportunities
 * Assist in the creation, maintenance and monitoring of credit policies, and
   procedures 
 * Employ best practices of data analysis and validation to ensure data accuracy
   and audit readiness
 * Translate analytical findings into clear, concise summaries for leadership
   audiences
 * Support preparation of materials for Leadership,  Committees and Board
   reporting
 * Conduct ad-hoc research projects including data collection, analysis and
   presentation of results
 * Develop working knowledge of credit decisioning systems, underwriting
   workflows and servicing impacts
    


QUALIFICATIONS

What makes you an ideal candidate?

 * Working knowledge of data analysis, reporting and visualization techniques
 * Strong analytical aptitude with ability to connect data trends to credit
   outcomes
 * Understanding of consumer credit fundamentals and willingness to develop
   underwriting judgment
 * High attention to detail and strong data accuracy discipline
 * Effective written and verbal communication skills
 * Ability to manage multiple priorities in a deadline-driven environment
 * Proficient with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and Word
 * Experience working with large datasets and complex spreadsheets
 * Exposure to SQL, SAS, Power BI, Databricks or similar tools preferred
   (training supported)
    

Experience and Education

 * 0–2 years of experience working with complex Excel workbooks, querying large
   multi-table datasets, data analysis, and data presentation; experience in
   consumer loan or lease portfolio analysis, reporting and/or forecasting
 * Bachelor’s Degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Mathematics, Business
   Analytics, MIS or related quantitative field required
    

Additional Knowledge and Skills

Working effectively within an AI enabled environment:  

 * Ability to use AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot) to support daily work
 * Skills in evaluating AI outputs for accuracy, compliance, and bias
 * Experience integrating AI into workflows to improve efficiency or insights
 * Familiarity with AI assisted research, summarization, and content generation
 * Understanding of responsible AI use, including ethics and data protection 

 

What We Offer: Generous benefits package available on day one to include: 401K
matching, bonding leave for new parents (12 weeks, 100% paid), tuition
assistance, training, GM employee auto discount, community service pay and nine
company holidays.

Our Culture: Our team members define and shape our culture — an environment that
welcomes innovative ideas, fosters integrity, and creates a sense of community
and belonging. Here we do more than work — we thrive.

Compensation: Competitive pay and bonus eligibility.

Work Life Balance: Hybrid, 2-3 days/week in the office; relocation assistance is
not available for this position.

NOTE: We are unable to consider candidates who require visa sponsorship for this
position

This position is not open to agency submissions

title: Senior Manager, Accounting
ai_core_responsibilities: The Senior Manager, Accounting leads the day-to-day execution of North America accounting operations, including close activities and financial reporting. They are responsible for managing the accounting team, ensuring strong internal controls, and driving process improvements across the organization.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a Bachelor's degree in Accounting and at least 8 years of progressive accounting experience, including team leadership. Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP, SOX requirements, and experience with complex monthly closes are essential for this role.
description_text:
WeightWatchers is a global digital health company. 
WeightWatchers is a global digital health company and the world’s #1 doctor-recommended, clinically studied behavioral weight health program. For sixty years, we have led the industry by blending science and community to help millions of people build sustainable healthy habits.
As the science of weight health rapidly evolves, so does WeightWatchers. We are redefining the category by developing new clinical pathways for GLP-1 medication access, creating specialized behavioral programs for members on weight-loss medications, and integrating medical care with our proven habit-change framework. By combining these clinical breakthroughs with our digital-first community, we are uniquely positioned to lead the future of weight health care.
Who We Are 
The WeightWatchers Finance Team serves as a core driver of the company's business success. This team of experienced financial professionals leverages data analytics and best practices to deliver insightful financial reporting and analysis. These contributions empower strategic decision-making across the organization, ensuring the company's financial health and sustainability.
The Role
The Senior Manager, Accounting is a critical leadership role responsible for the day-to-day execution, quality, and continued transformation of Weight Watchers' North America accounting operations. Reporting to the North America Controller, this person will lead the team responsible for operating expenses and related close activities, while ensuring timely and accurate financial reporting, strong internal controls, and audit-ready support.
This is a hands-on role for a leader who can create clarity in a complex environment by setting ownership, establishing review discipline, developing the team, resolving issues before they become close blockers, and building scalable processes across evolving offerings. The successful candidate will combine strong accounting judgment with practical operating leadership to serve as a key partner in running the North America accounting function.
What you wil do
Accounting Operations and Close
Lead the day-to-day execution of North America general accounting and operating expense close activities, including managing the close calendar, dependencies, status reporting, issue escalation, and delivery against the company’s close timeline.
Oversee the preparation and review of journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, account analyses, and supporting schedules, with a strong focus on completeness, accuracy, and clear audit trails.
Maintain a detailed understanding of key accounting flows across U.S. and Canada operations, including payroll and benefits, leases, fixed assets, prepaids and accruals, marketing and other operating expenses, intercompany, cash, franchise arrangements, and other assigned general accounting areas.
Drive disciplined variance and flux analysis and partner with FP&A and business stakeholders to explain results and identify emerging risks early.
Act as the day-to-day escalation point for accounting issues, making sound decisions, documenting conclusions, and bringing material or complex matters to the North America Controller with a clear recommendation.
People Leadership and Team Development
Lead and develop a multi-level accounting team that includes managers and individual contributors across general accounting, revenue, and accounts receivable operations.
Establish clear roles, decision rights, performance expectations, and review standards; ensure work is appropriately assigned and that accountability sits at the right level.
Provide timely, direct feedback and meaningful coaching, while building technical depth, business understanding, cross-training, and succession coverage across the team.
Create an environment that values ownership, transparency, curiosity, collaboration, and continuous improvement, while maintaining high standards for execution and follow-through.
Balance leadership with hands-on involvement: step into complex work when needed, but build durable processes and team capability rather than becoming a single point of dependency.
Who you are
Bachelor's degree in Accounting.
8+ years of progressive accounting experience, including meaningful experience leading accounting teams and owning a complex monthly and quarterly close.
Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP and experience overseeing general accounting areas such as accruals, operating expenses, payroll, leases, fixed assets, intercompany, and balance sheet accounting.
Demonstrated experience reviewing journal entries, reconciliations, financial analyses, and audit support with a high standard for completeness, accuracy, and documentation.
Strong understanding of internal controls and SOX requirements in a public company environment.
Experience driving process improvement, clarifying ownership, and strengthening team capability in an environment with changing systems, processes, and priorities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate accounting issues into clear decisions, actions, and risks for both finance and non-finance stakeholders.
Strong judgment, organization, and follow-through. Ability to manage competing deadlines, challenge work constructively, and escalate issues early with proposed solutions.
Preferred
CPA strongly preferred
Combination of public accounting and public company industry experience
Experience with subscription, digital consumer, healthcare or clinical, marketplace, or other high-volume transaction environments
Experience with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, familiarity with Workday, Looker, FCCS, or similar systems a plus
Base salary may vary depending on, but not limited to: skills, experience, and location. This role is also eligible for a comprehensive benefits package and annual bonus program.
US Pay Range
$130,000—$145,000 USD

description_text:
HeartLand, LLC is seeking a highly motivated and customer-driven professional to
join our growing East Regional Accounting team as a Staff
Accountant in Philadelphia, PA. 

  

The Company 

HeartLand, LLC is a progressive organization dedicated to building relationships
and delivering exceptional service through leading commercial landscape firms
across the US.  We deliver the ordinary in extraordinary ways, by operating our
business with a shared vision of excellence – combining best practices and the
right tools for the job with ongoing training and support. We acquire companies
in attractive markets who share a common culture of excellence and success.  Our
landscape companies are the first choice for employees and clients in the
markets they serve.  

  

The Opportunity: 

The Regional Staff Accountant is responsible for various accounting functions as
directed by the Regional Controller.  The Staff Accountant focuses on managing
the general ledger within Acumatica, our ERP system, reconciling account
balances, and performing month-end close procedures.  The Staff Accountant will
also demonstrate proficiency in spotting errors and suggest ways to improve
efficiency. 

  

The position reports to the Regional Controller, and focuses on the following
two areas: 

  

General Ledger & Month-End Close 

 * Monitor general ledger activity and execute month-end close processes 

 * Track and reconcile bank activity throughout the month 

 * Record non-A/R deposits 

 * Record payroll-related entries 

 * Calculate and post accruals 

 * Reconcile financial activity between Aspire (production system) and Acumatica
   (accounting system); investigate and resolve variances 

 * Perform balance sheet account analysis and reconciliations 

 * Conduct expense analysis to ensure proper coding 

Reporting & Compliance 

 * Prepare monthly, quarterly, and year-end financial reports 

 * Review financial statements for completeness and accuracy and perform
   variance analysis 

 * Prepare and file sales and use tax returns, and process payments 

 * Compile and organize documentation for external audits 

Systems, Integration & Stakeholder Support 

 * Assist in the integration of new operating companies, including key
   onboarding tasks 

 * Maintain accurate data and effective controls across Aspire and Acumatica 

 * Ensure local collections activities are performed consistently; coordinate
   the referral of delinquent accounts to a collection agency as needed 

 * Analyze aged accounts and reserve bad debt in accordance with corporate
   policies 

 * Provide accounting support to the regional team, operating company
   management, and administrative staff 

Recordkeeping 

 * Maintain an organized filing system for accounts, statements, transactions,
   payments, and debts 

Key Performance Metrics 

The Regional Staff Accountant’s performance will be evaluated on accuracy,
timeliness, adherence to internal controls, and effective collaboration in
support of Heartland’s operational objectives. Specific measures include: 

 * Internal controls: Maintaining robust controls evidenced by a complete and
   timely tie-out between Aspire and Acumatica, with reconciling items
   identified and resolved 

 * Close quality and timeliness: Completing a full and accurate monthly
   financial close while meeting established deadlines 

 * Receivables management: Keeping aged receivables within thresholds
   established by Heartland Corporate 

 * Collaboration: Demonstrating a team-oriented approach by partnering
   constructively with departmental and operating company staff 

The Regional Staff Accountant will possess: 

The Regional Staff Accountant will: 

 * Exude the company’s values in all respects: 

 * Human – we do love plants, but we cultivate people to serve people 

 * Exceptional – our best efforts energize everything we do 

 * Accountable – we own the outcomes in our relationships with each other and
   our clients 

 * Respectful – we believe in the golden rule 

 * Trusted – clients know they can count on us to keep their best interests at
   heart 

 * Hold a bachelor’s degree and five years of accounting experience 

 * If no college degree, have a minimum of nine years of accounting work
   experience 

 * Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability to evolving accounting processes,
   systems, procedures, and technology 

 * Exhibit strict attention to detail, with exceptional time management,
   organizational, and follow-up skills 

 * Demonstrate a results-oriented approach with a proven ability to follow
   through while handling multiple and competing priorities 

 * Provide timely, high-quality support by communicating clearly, listening
   actively to clarify needs, applying sound judgment, and making well-reasoned
   decisions 

 * Approach the role with a solutions-oriented mindset toward opportunities and
   challenges 

Other Requirements 

 * Periodic local travel to other company offices may be necessary 

 * Occasional overnight travel may be required

title: Financial Controller

This role also involves leading the finance team, managing audit processes, and partnering with leadership to support organizational growth.

description_text:
Who We Are 
Rising Edge Group is an electrical contracting company founded in 2002, specialization in high-voltage electrical solutions that power critical infrastructure across North America. With operations in both Canada and the United States, we partner with clients across the electrical utilities, renewable energy, and industrial sectors to design, build, and maintain the critical infrastructure systems communities and industries rely on. 
Driven by a clear vision to strengthen the stability, reliability, and advancement of energy infrastructure, we take pride in delivering work that matters. Guided by our STRIDE values - Safety, Teamwork, Responsibility, Integrity, Deliver, and Excellence - we foster a people focused culture of growth, mentorship and collaboration where safety always come first. 
What You'll Do 
The US Financial Controller is responsible for overseeing accounting operations, financial reporting, internal controls, audit coordination, regulatory compliance, and tax compliance activities for the U.S. business. This role works collaboratively with the Canadian Financial Controller to ensure the integrity of financial information, compliance with U.S. GAAP and applicable regulations, and support executive leadership with accurate and timely financial insights. The Controller partners closely with Operations to maintain a strong control environment and support organizational growth.
Key Responsibilities
The responsibilities include, but may not be limited to: 
Financial Reporting & Accounting
Drive the month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close processes to ensure timely and accurate financial reporting.
Prepare and review financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP and company policies.
Ensure accuracy and completeness of general ledger activities, account reconciliations, accruals, and journal entries.
Develop and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and internal controls.
Analyze financial results and provide meaningful commentary on variances, trends, and key performance indicators.
Support budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning activities.
Internal & External Audit Support
Serve as the primary point of contact for auditors.
Coordinate annual financial statement audits and periodic reviews.
Manage audit requests and ensure timely delivery of supporting documentation.
Monitor and remediate audit findings and control deficiencies.
Maintain documentation and evidence supporting compliance with internal control frameworks.
Partner with business leaders to strengthen governance and control processes.
Regulatory Compliance
Ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local financial reporting requirements.
Monitor changes in accounting standards, regulations, and reporting requirements and assess business impacts.
Oversee maintenance of statutory records and regulatory filings.
Collaborate with Legal, Compliance, and Finance teams to address emerging regulatory matters.
Tax Compliance
Oversee U.S. federal, state, and local tax compliance processes.
Coordinate preparation and filing of income, sales and use, property, franchise, and other applicable taxes.
Partner with external tax advisors and service providers on tax reporting and planning matters.
Ensure accurate tax accounting, tax provisions, and supporting schedules.
Support tax audits and inquiries from regulatory authorities.
Identify opportunities to improve tax processes and strengthen compliance controls.
Leadership & Business Partnership
Build out US team to support business growth
Lead, develop, and mentor accounting and finance team members.
Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
Partner with business leaders to provide financial guidance and support decision-making.
Drive process improvements, automation initiatives, and best practices across finance operations.
Support special projects as needed.
Additional Information 
As a condition of employment, candidates will be required to complete pre-employment screening including professional reference checks and a criminal record check.
What We're Looking For 
Education
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field required.
CPA designation strongly preferred.
Master's degree in Accounting, Finance, or Business Administration is a plus.
Experience
8+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience.
3+ years of leadership experience managing accounting or finance teams.
Strong experience with financial reporting, external audits, and regulatory compliance.
Experience overseeing U.S. tax compliance and working with external tax advisors.
Experience in a multi-entity or complex business environment preferred.
Public accounting experience is desirable.
Technical Skills
Advanced knowledge of U.S. GAAP.
Strong understanding of internal controls and audit requirements.
Knowledge of federal, state, and local tax regulations.
Experience with ERP systems (Vista by Viewpoint preferred).
Advanced Excel and financial analysis skills.
Experience with financial reporting and consolidation systems preferred.
Competencies
Strong leadership and people management skills.
Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
High level of integrity, professionalism, and accountability.
Ability to collaborate effectively across functions and with senior leadership.
What We Offer
Competitive compensation with weekly pay periods 
Generous paid time off 
401(k) employer matching 
Comprehensive benefits package (medical, dental and vision) 
Company-paid safety training 
Ongoing training, development, and career advancement opportunities 
Employee Family Assistance Program (confidential counselling support) 
Employee Referral Bonus Program 
Why Rising Edge Group? 
Safety & Excellence: Safety is at the heart of everything we do. Every project is approached with diligence, strategic planning, and reliable execution practices to protect our teams and the clients we serve while delivering world-class high-voltage solutions. Our unwavering commitment to safety and quality drives excellence on every project, every day. 
People-First Culture: You’re more than a job title. Every person contributes to powering essential energy infrastructure across North America. Our teams are built on collaboration, respect, and accountability. We support our employees through meaningful engagement initiatives, team events, and a culture that prioritizes wellbeing, inclusion, and genuine lasting connections. 
Career Growth & Impact: Your role is a path to a long-term career. We empower our employees with hands-on experience, exposure to diverse projects, and opportunities to advance across disciplines, locations, and career paths. Through continuous learning, mentorship, and professional development, you’ll build lasting expertise while making a tangible impact in an environment where teamwork and integrity guide our work. 
Reward & Recognition: We believe skill, dedication, and excellence deserves recognition. Competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and a strong culture of appreciation ensure your achievements are celebrated, your growth is supported, and your work truly makes a difference. 
At Rising Edge Group, you’re not just building projects, you’re building a meaningful career where your work helps power the future, one project at a time.

title: Financial Analyst
ai_core_responsibilities: The Financial Analyst supports the Finance Department through recurring financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and profitability analysis. They also assist with enterprise decision-making by developing financial models and performing liquidity and risk management analysis.
ai_requirements_summary: Candidates must have a bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field along with one to three years of relevant experience. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and a strong understanding of GAAP and financial analysis principles are required.
description_text:
Description
Job Summary Overview
The Financial Analyst supports the Finance Department through recurring financial reporting, budgeting and forecasting, profitability analysis, financial modeling, liquidity management, asset/liability management (ALM), interest rate risk (IRR) analysis, pricing analysis, and other analytical initiatives.

Working under the direction of the VP of Finance and in partnership with the Strategic Finance Manager, the Financial Analyst prepares reports, analyzes financial and operational data, develops financial models, supports forecasting activities, and assists with enterprise decision-making through accurate and timely analysis. The position provides support for management reporting, ALCO reporting, Board reporting, budgeting, profitability analysis, liquidity management, capital planning, enterprise risk reporting, and other Finance Department responsibilities.

The Financial Analyst is expected to develop analytical expertise across multiple Finance disciplines while providing professional and timely support to internal business partners.

Essential Job Functions
Collaborates across business lines and communicates effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
Assists in preparing timely and accurate financial reports for management, committees, and the Board of Directors.
Assists in the preparation of monthly financial reporting packages, ALCO materials, pricing analyses, investment reporting, profitability reporting, and other recurring Finance deliverables.
Performs income and expense variance analysis and assists with earnings, balance sheet, capital, and liquidity forecasting.
Supports product, channel, portfolio, and organizational profitability reporting and analysis.
Supports pricing analysis and recommendation development for deposit, lending, and fee-based products.
Assists with business case development, ROI analysis, financial feasibility studies, and scenario modeling for products, projects, and strategic initiatives.
Supports liquidity management activities through daily, monthly, and quarterly cash flow forecasting and monitoring.
Assists with ALM and IRR modeling, including data preparation, validation, assumption maintenance, documentation, and results analysis.
Supports investment accounting, investment reporting, collateral maintenance, and related reconciliations.
Assists in the annual budgeting process, ongoing financial forecasting, and budget reporting.
Develops and maintains financial models, reports, dashboards, and analytical tools used to support decision making.
Validates source data, investigates variances and anomalies, and maintains appropriate documentation supporting Finance processes and analyses.
Assists with enterprise risk reporting, CECL monitoring, audit support, regulatory examinations, policy reviews, and other compliance-related activities.
Cross-trains across Finance Department responsibilities and provides backup support for recurring functions.
Acquires and applies knowledge of the credit union, its products, systems, and processes to resolve issues and deliver high-quality work product.
Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

Requirements
Position Required Qualifications

Minimum Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Analytics, or a related field and one (1) to three (3) years of experience in financial analysis, accounting, auditing, banking, credit unions, or a comparable analytical role; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications.
Knowledge of financial analysis, accounting principles, and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
Ability to analyze large datasets, identify patterns, trends, and anomalies, and communicate findings clearly.
Ability to build, maintain, validate, and document financial models used for forecasting, budgeting, profitability analysis, liquidity management, and strategic decision support.
Ability to develop reports, dashboards, and recurring analytical processes.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
Professional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and work independently with minimal supervision.

Licenses, Training, and Certifications Required
None.

Preferred Qualifications
Experience in a credit union, bank, or other financial institution. 
Experience with budgeting, forecasting, profitability analysis, pricing analysis, financial modeling, or business case development. 
Experience with Power BI, SQL, data visualization tools, or similar analytical platforms. 
Experience with Empyrean, Symitar, Jack Henry, Great Plains, Visible Equity, Acumatica, or related financial reporting systems. 
Experience with ALM modeling applications. 
Experience supporting investment accounting, investment reporting, collateral reporting, or fixed-income portfolio analytics. 
Experience preparing analysis, reports, or presentation materials for management committees, executive leadership, or Boards of Directors.


Hybrid Work Environment and Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to reach with hands and arms. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand or sit; use hands to finger keys accurately when using calculator machines or computer keyboards. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distant vision, and peripheral vision. The noise level in the work environment is quiet. Must be able to travel independently to department and branch locations.


NOTE: The job description is intended to be generic in nature. It is not an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities. Requirements listed in the above qualifications and physical requirements are representative of the knowledge, skill, abilities, physical demands, or work environment required or encountered that must be met by an employee to successfully perform each duty and each function of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.


Employees who work from home must have business operational internet to complete work tasks and communicate via video call or chat messaging systems in a dedicated workspace.

Description
The Financial Controller will undertake all aspects of financial management, including corporate accounting, regulatory and financial reporting, periodic budget and cashflow forecast preparation, and the development of internal control policies and procedures. Requirements
Assist the Chief Operating Officer (COO) in establishing, monitoring, and enforcing accounting policies and procedures and financial controls across all divisions and projects in accordance with the company’s procedures.

Coordinate with the Travel Administrator to ensure that travel guidelines and operational procedures are updated to enhance overall efficiency throughout the organization.
Coordinate with all Divisional Finance Directors to communicate operational updates and understand risk mitigation issues identified.

description_text:
WHAT IS BOX? 
Box (NYSE:BOX) is the leader in Intelligent Content Management. Our platform enables organizations to fuel collaboration, manage the entire content lifecycle, secure critical content, and transform business workflows with enterprise AI. We help companies thrive in the new AI-first era of business. Founded in 2005, Box simplifies work for leading global organizations, including JLL, Morgan Stanley, and Nationwide. Box is headquartered in Redwood City, CA, with offices across the United States, Europe, and Asia.
By joining Box, you will have the unique opportunity to continue driving our platform forward. Content powers how we work. It’s the billions of files and information flowing across teams, departments, and key business processes every single day: contracts, invoices, employee records, financials, product specs, marketing assets, and more. Our mission is to bring intelligence to the world of content management and empower our customers to completely transform workflows across their organizations. With the combination of AI and enterprise content, the opportunity has never been greater to transform how the world works together and at Box you will be on the front lines of this massive shift.
WHY BOX NEEDS YOU 
Box's Tax team is growing, and we're looking for a Senior Tax Accountant to own our indirect tax function. In this role, you will be the subject matter expert for sales and use tax across Box's US and global operations — ensuring compliance, driving process improvements, and partnering cross-functionally with Finance, Legal, and Revenue Operations to support the business as it scales.
You will work in a collaborative, high-impact environment where your expertise directly shapes how Box manages its indirect tax obligations. This is an opportunity to bring both technical depth and strategic thinking to a team that values accuracy, efficiency, and continuous improvement.
WHAT YOU'LL DO 
Manage end-to-end sales and use tax compliance, including preparation, review, and timely filing of returns across all applicable US jurisdictions.

Partner with Revenue Operations and Billing to ensure accurate tax calculation and collection within Box's billing systems and CPQ tools.

description_text:
POSITION SUMMARY:

The Accounts Payable Coordinator is responsible for reviewing, processing, and initiating payments for all AP related transactions across multiple entities. The position processes transactions for multiple subsidiaries and initiates payments from multiple bank accounts. Typical responsibilities include processing vendor invoices, purchase requisitions, purchase orders, expense reports, pack slips, and manages supporting documentation. This position is expected to operate independently with minimal direct supervision from the Accounting Manager by following established procedures and guidelines to perform the job's essential functions.

 

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

 * Processes all vendor invoices by matching requisitions, purchase orders, and packing slips. 
 * Processes all non-purchase order-related invoices. 
 * Verifies that invoices have appropriate authorization and supporting documentation prior to payment processing. 
 * Codes invoices and expense reports with cost center and general ledger account numbers. 
 * Maintains organized files for historical data that can be easily referenced as needed.
 * Assists with maintaining the employee expense reports policy and procedures. 
 * Processes all employee expense reports. 
 * Processes all travel advances for SCC travelers.
 * Responsible for automated and manual check printing and distribution. 
 * Answers all vendor inquiries (external & internal). 
 * Acts as a backup auditor of SCC’s internal lunch program and lunch vendor invoices, including reconciliation of cash related to the lunch program. 
 * Obtains approval of invoices by proper management when required. 
 * Enters AP related journal entries in ERP system (Netsuite).
 * Assists in general ledger & spend review as a part of month-end close process.
 * Prepares and files all annual Form 1099s. 
 * Assists with gathering data for annual audits. 
 * Assists with budget research and explanation for all business units. 
 * Provides additional accounting support to the Accounting Manager and Controller as needed. 
 * Ensures strict confidentiality of financial records. 
 * Complies with all approved procedures, directives and guidelines. 
 * Performs other duties as assigned.




Education Required:

 * High School Diploma required.
 * Associate’s or BS in Accounting, Finance, or a related field highly preferred.




Experience Required:

 * Minimum of three years of AP or related accounting experience.
 * Intermediate MS Office skills.
 * Experience with NetSuite or a comparable ERP system preferred.




Skills Required:

 * Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
 * Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
 * Strong organizational and time-management skills.
 * Effective written and verbal communication skills.
 * Ability to research and resolve invoice, payment, and vendor discrepancies.
 * Proficiency with MS Office, particularly Excel.
 * Ability to maintain confidentiality of financial and employee information.
 * Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, multi-entity environment.

title: Financial Planning and Analysis Manager
ai_core_responsibilities: The FP&A Manager leads forecasting, budgeting, and long-range financial planning to support strategic business decisions. They also manage cash flow visibility, risk management, and provide actionable financial insights to senior management.

description_text:
Location: Rochester, New York

Department: Finance

Reports to: Director of Finance

Work arrangement: On-site

Travel: None required

Compensation: The target hiring range is generally $130,000–$155,000, depending on relevant experience, skills, education, internal equity, and business needs. This role is eligible for QED's annual performance-based incentive program with a target opportunity of 15% of base salary, as well as a comprehensive benefits package and 401(k) program.


ABOUT QED TECHNOLOGIES

At QED Technologies, we are building what's next.

For 30 years, QED has helped customers solve complex challenges in precision optics through advanced fabrication and metrology technologies. Our proprietary solutions support applications across aerospace and defense, semiconductor manufacturing, space and astronomy, research, fusion, and other advanced industries.

Our work depends on talented people who bring curiosity, precision, collaboration, and ownership to difficult problems. We are building a high-performing culture where people are trusted to make an impact, teams work across boundaries, and continuous improvement is part of how we operate.


THE OPPORTUNITY

The FP&A Manager helps QED Technologies Rochester (QTR) make sound, well-informed financial decisions by leading forecasting, budgeting, long-range planning, and cash flow visibility across the business.

Reporting to the Director of Finance, this individual-contributor role partners closely with senior management and functional leaders to understand business performance, identify trends and opportunities, and translate financial data into clear, actionable insight. You will own the monthly forecasting and annual budgeting processes, maintain a rolling 26-week cash flow forecast, and lead long-range financial planning that supports QTR's strategic objectives. The role also carries responsibility for risk management, insurance programs, and customer letters of credit and bank guarantees.

This is more than a reporting role. The successful candidate will bring strong financial judgment, analytical rigor, and the ability to communicate complex financial information clearly to senior stakeholders. You will be comfortable balancing recurring deadlines with ad hoc analysis, working independently across multiple priorities, and building the models, dashboards, and KPIs that help QTR run its business with confidence.


WHAT YOU WILL DO


FORECASTING, BUDGETING, AND PLANNING

 * Lead the monthly forecasting process, including revenue, expenses, cash flow, and key operating metrics.
 * Own the annual budgeting and planning process, partnering with business leaders to develop realistic, data-driven financial plans.
 * Lead the long-range financial planning process, developing multi-year financial models and forecasts that align with the company's strategic objectives, evaluate growth opportunities, and provide senior management with insights to support long-term business decisions.
 * Maintain a rolling 26-week cash flow forecast, providing visibility into liquidity, working capital, and near-term cash requirements.


REPORTING, ANALYSIS, AND BUSINESS PARTNERSHIP

 * Prepare and deliver monthly financial reporting packages, including variance analysis against budget, forecast, and prior-year performance.
 * Analyze financial and operational results to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and drivers of business performance.
 * Partner with senior management and functional leaders to translate financial data into actionable insights and support key business decisions.
 * Design and develop financial models, analyses, dashboards, and other tools to support strategic and operational decision-making.
 * Develop ad hoc analyses and scenario modeling to evaluate business opportunities, investments, cost initiatives, and other strategic decisions.
 * Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), providing meaningful analysis and recommendations to management.
 * Collaborate cross-functionally with Accounting, Operations, Sales, and other teams to improve financial visibility, planning, and accountability.


RISK, TREASURY, AND CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

 * Oversee risk management and insurance programs, including identifying and assessing key business risks, maintaining appropriate insurance coverage, coordinating renewals and claims, and partnering with internal and external stakeholders to mitigate financial and operational exposure.
 * Manage customer letters of credit and bank guarantees, ensuring timely issuance, renewal, amendment, tracking, and release, and maintaining appropriate financial security in accordance with customer contracts and company requirements.
 * Identify opportunities to improve business operations, profitability, cash flow, and overall financial performance.
 * Continuously improve FP&A processes, reporting, forecasting methodologies, and financial models to increase efficiency and accuracy.
 * Communicate financial results and recommendations clearly and effectively to senior management and other stakeholders.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 * Senior management receives timely, accurate, and actionable financial insight that supports confident decision-making.
 * Monthly forecasts, annual budgets, and long-range plans are grounded in realistic, data-driven assumptions and delivered on schedule.
 * The 26-week cash flow forecast provides reliable visibility into liquidity and working capital needs.
 * Financial reporting packages and variance analysis are clear, accurate, and delivered consistently each month.
 * Business risks are identified early, insurance coverage remains appropriate, and letters of credit and bank guarantees are managed without lapses or compliance issues.
 * Cross-functional partners across Accounting, Operations, and Sales view the FP&A function as a trusted, responsive partner in business decisions.
 * FP&A processes, models, and reporting continue to improve in efficiency and accuracy over time.


WHAT YOU BRING

 * Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field; MBA or relevant advanced degree is a plus.
 * Five or more years of progressive experience in FP&A, financial analysis, corporate finance, or a related field.
 * Strong experience with financial forecasting, annual budgeting, and variance analysis.
 * Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, with the ability to translate complex data into clear business insights.
 * Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience working with financial reporting, planning, and ERP systems.
 * Strong understanding of financial statements, accounting principles, and the relationship between the P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow.
 * Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to effectively communicate financial insights and recommendations to senior management.
 * Strong business judgment and problem-solving skills, with a demonstrated ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
 * Highly detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
 * Ability to balance attention to detail with a broader understanding of business strategy and operational objectives.
 * Ability to manage recurring deadlines while remaining responsive to ad hoc requests.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 * Experience partnering with cross-functional teams and influencing business decisions through financial analysis.
 * Eagerness to learn and develop treasury expertise, including letters of credit, bank guarantees, and risk and insurance management.
 * Experience in a manufacturing, engineering, aerospace, defense, or similarly regulated environment.
 * Team-oriented, proactive, and comfortable operating as an individual contributor with broad cross-functional visibility.

The Accounting Manager reports directly to the Controller and helps establish
shared accounting services for the mortgage, title, and title insurance
businesses. This hands-on role owns assigned close and reporting work, guides
accounting staff, and helps build clear, efficient procedures as the team grows.
